note_out: Recursive self-improvement connects singularity scenarios to modern AI-risk arguments, but the specific lineage is broader than one source.
Routledge identifies L’Homme machine as a materialist manifesto applying materialism explicitly to human beings.
Functionalism commonly develops within physicalist philosophy of mind, though it is not logically committed to physicalism.
SEP says Turing’s work was explicitly invoked and inspired Putnam’s machine-state theories in early functionalism.
SEP presents the Chinese room as an argument against computational accounts of mind and understanding.
SEP discusses Block’s absent-qualia and Chinese-nation objections as major challenges to functionalism.
Dennett’s consciousness theory is routinely classified as broadly functionalist, though his account is not reducible to generic functionalism.
SEP states Chalmers argues structural or functional explanations leave phenomenal consciousness unexplained.
Thagard explicitly argues energy’s dependence on material substrates undermines substrate independence and mind-body functionalism.
Seth challenges computation’s sufficiency and argues consciousness depends on being a living organism.
The paper explicitly calls the abstraction fallacy a physically grounded refutation of computational functionalism.
The review says Chirimuuta rejects inferring machine consciousness by mistaking computational models for the brain they simplify.
Seth explicitly credits Searle’s original biological naturalism, while adopting a broader life-based version.
Nagel’s what-it-is-like formulation is a standard precursor to Chalmers’s hard problem, but direct dependence is not established here.
SEP treats Nagel’s what-it-is-like argument as centrally concerning the subjective qualitative character of experience.
SEP explicitly describes Levine’s explanatory gap as the problem of explaining qualia in physical terms.
The explanatory gap is a standard precursor to the hard problem, though Chalmers’s argument is not simply Levine’s renamed.
Leibniz’s mill anticipates an explanatory concern, but calling it the hard problem in 1714 is retrospective interpretation.
The mill and Chinese room are commonly compared as internal-observer arguments, but differ in target and conclusion.
Chalmers has prominently explored panpsychist and panprotopsychist responses to the hard problem; this is standard scholarship.
SEP discusses McGinn’s cognitive-closure claim alongside stronger explanatory-gap positions and Chalmers’s anti-physicalist argument.
Frankish explicitly replaces Chalmers’s hard problem with the illusion problem by denying phenomenal realism.
Frankish names Dennett as illusionism’s pre-eminent defender.
Dennett explicitly argues Chalmers’s hard problem misdirects inquiry and should be dissolved by functional scientific work.
Hofstadter and Dennett jointly edited The Mind’s I and supplied commentary on mind, self, and information processing.
The journal abstract explicitly describes Hofstadter’s Gödelian proposal linking incompleteness-style self-reference to consciousness and mental causation.
IEP details Penrose’s Gödelian argument that no formal system can capture human mathematical reasoning.
The Orch OR paper explicitly proposes quantum computation in neuronal microtubules.
Koch moved from NCC research to prominent advocacy and development of IIT, but the theory was originated by Tononi.
Crick and Koch explicitly proposed 40–70 Hz synchronized oscillations binding features as a mechanism of visual awareness.
IEP details Aaronson’s reductio: simple expander graphs or grids can receive implausibly high phi.
Tegmark explicitly generalizes Tononi’s IIT and proposes consciousness as a state of matter, perceptronium.
IEP explains IIT’s attribution of minimal consciousness to simple systems and its panpsychist implications.
Bengio explicitly says the consciousness prior is anchored in Global Workspace Theory.
Butlin et al. derive four AI-consciousness indicators directly from Global Workspace Theory.
Butlin et al. explicitly survey higher-order theories and derive corresponding AI-consciousness indicators.
Graziano calls HOT a close cousin of AST while distinguishing representation of an item from representation of attention.
The paper maps GWT’s unconscious specialized processors to Minsky’s agents.
The source explicitly compares Freud’s unconscious primary process with Kahneman’s largely unconscious System 1.
The article explicitly equates Haidt’s elephant and rider with Kahneman’s System 1 and System 2.
Seth explicitly develops his account using Friston’s free-energy principle and predictive models of bodily regulation.
Seth’s embodied, interoceptive account strongly aligns with Damasio’s body-regulation account, but direct dependence was not explicit in opened sources.
Damasio explicitly uses James’s bodily-perception assumptions as a stepping stone for his account of emotional feeling.
Fields’s generic bounded-system FEP work is from 2021–2022, not the 2012 point claimed here.
Levin’s publication list documents numerous Fields–Levin coauthored papers from 2018 onward.
Westworld’s creators explicitly name Julian Jaynes among their guides on consciousness.
Hoffman’s conscious realism is nonphysicalist monism, but he distinguishes it from historical idealisms rather than presenting it as their extension.
Metzinger denies substantial selves; Frankish illusionism denies phenomenal properties. They are thematically related but target different claims.
The source explicitly says Kegan’s neo-Piagetian theory extends cognitive development across the adult lifespan.
The page states Leary read Huxley after his first psilocybin experience, found corroboration, and then befriended him.
Both invoke nonclassical or quantum ideas in brain theories, but use distinct mechanisms and no direct influence was found.
Seth and Friston explicitly frame interoceptive inference in enactivist, embodied terms tied to bodily regulation.
Bostrom explicitly uses The Matrix as the popular point of entry to his simulation argument.
Permutation City explores software minds and simulated reality, but no direct connection to Bostrom’s argument was found.
Blindsight separates intelligence from consciousness; illusionism instead disputes phenomenal properties. The overlap is thematic, not the same thesis.
